senses.sense_definition: A biological ancestor or forefather, especially the founder of a family, dynasty, or tribe.

examples.text: He traced his lineage back to a wealthy <w>progenitor</w> who settled the region centuries ago.
Historical records indicate that the ancient warrior was the common <w>progenitor</w> of several noble families.

senses.sense_definition: A predecessor, precursor, or early model from which later versions or innovations develop.

examples.text: Many historians consider the early mainframe computer to be the direct <w>progenitor</w> of modern personal computers.
The experimental novel served as a notable <w>progenitor</w> of the modernist literary movement.

senses.sense_definition: A person who originates, initiates, or founds a system, idea, or artistic movement.

examples.text: The philosopher is widely regarded as the <w>progenitor</w> of modern democratic theory.
She was celebrated as a courageous <w>progenitor</w> of the new wave in independent cinema.

senses.sense_definition: An ancestral organism, species, or stem form from which other evolutionary lines or cell types arise.

examples.text: Biologists believe that this fossil represents the evolutionary <w>progenitor</w> of modern birds.
The laboratory study focused on how stem cells differentiate from an initial <w>progenitor</w> in neural tissue.
